name: Horizon Reclaim (India) Limited
sector: Reclaimed rubber, waste-tyre recycling and emerging pyrolysis products
summary: Strong physical revenue growth and received IPO funding support expansion, but normalized cash returns, new-plant execution and historical control weaknesses warrant caution. The funded base yields 7.90% against a 15% hurdle at ₹139.50; survival is not the same as shareholder downside protection.

score_note: Exact canonical weights, no overrides. BQS 5.54, GQS 6.70 and IAS 3.885 before one-decimal display. IAS is conditional on the ₹5 lakh liquidity reference and the explicit assumed cash bridge.

gates.reason: Primary disclosures reveal historical filing omissions and accounting/control weaknesses, but reviewed sources do not establish promoter abuse, fraud or current default. Unmodified audit is acknowledged without treating it as a clean bill of health.

Balance-sheet claims and forecast cash identities reconcile. Original, restated and later statutory versions are kept separate; quantified inventory/AR issues and legal claims have bounded sensitivities. The corrected H1 primary PDF is unavailable, so its secondary headline is not used as audited cash or a score upgrade.

Received IPO money is restricted to approved uses. After the common modeled pre-cutoff path, a source-grounded ₹44 crore physical run rate, zero EPR, 12% initial physical margin, 75-day inventory and 60-day receivables survive without rescue. Optional unplaced machinery is curtailed without releasing its pool; existing commitments, debt, tax and benefits are paid. Completing all remaining machinery also survives that restrained case. Construction overruns may need pacing or finance; this is not asserted as an actual default.

Sixty post-listing historical observations and an eligible 1,200-share market lot support coarse tradability, not live executability. Price and turnover are secondary/proxy evidence, and no current BSE surveillance or two-sided depth clearance is claimed.

sections.title: 1. Executive verdict
sections.text:
Horizon Reclaim has demonstrated genuine physical-business growth, not merely a recycling-policy narrative. Revenue rose from ₹13.37 crore in FY2021 to ₹49.42 crore in FY2026. Excluding the newer sale of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) credits, physical-product revenue reached ₹46.32 crore. The received June IPO materially improves funding, but new plants, inventory conversion and operating controls remain the central tests. This is an execution-led expansion candidate, not an established compounder. [S1][S2][S3][S6]

At the secondary 19 October close of ₹139.50, the funded five-year base gives 7.90% annualized equity return against a 15% hurdle. The bear case is funded but ends near ₹51.52 per share, about 63% below entry. Survival and investment attractiveness are different questions: a no-rescue operating stress survives, while the share valuation still has substantial downside. The evidence does not support buying simply because stated capacity is expanding several-fold. [S15]

sections.title: 2. Research header and evidence boundary
sections.text:
Research cutoff: 20 October 2026. Last market session: 19 October. Issuer: Horizon Reclaim (India) Limited; ISIN INE1SEO01013; BSE code 544794; BSE SME. Current issued shares are 19,515,400 and the verified lot is 1,200 shares. The official HORIZON$ permitted-to-trade row is not a separate NSE listing. At the reference price one lot costs ₹167,400. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is illustrative, not the user's allocation. [S2][S8][S15][S16][S17]

The archetype is capital-intensive, commodity-linked recycling manufacturing, with separately identified EPR revenue and emerging pyrolysis operations. All financial quantities are INR crore unless stated otherwise. Original FY2021–23 accounts, restated FY2024–26 prospectus accounts and the later statutory annual presentation are distinguished. Primary faces are well supported; governance, cash comparability, current funding and implementation confidence are Medium. Forecast uncertainty is High.

The 19 October corrected H1 update is indexed as ₹28.17 crore revenue, up 28.24%. The signed BSE PDF returned HTTP 403, while the issuer's reviewed document list did not contain it. Consequently, this is a secondary corroboration of a management update, not audited H1 revenue or cash. It does not determine the revenue-factor uplift or establish current debt and free cash. [S12][S13][S14]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and gates
sections.text:
BQS is 5.54, displayed 5.5; GQS is 6.70, displayed 6.7; IAS is 3.885, displayed 3.9. Factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP 6, CASH 5, BAL 6, EXEC 6, EARN 6; IAS factors R 2, D 4, P 4 and L 6. Exact canonical weights, unrounded arithmetic, evidence links and confidence are retained in the audit. No missing factor is filled with a neutral score or reweighted. No historical factor is 9–10.

G1 is Conditional: historical corporate, accounting and control deficiencies are material, but reviewed evidence does not establish abuse, fraud or a current default. G2 is Conditional: source versions and quantified issues are separated and bounded rather than concealed. G3 is Conditional: approved IPO uses and a credible reduced-growth case fund existing obligations without assumed rescue. G4 is Conditional: historical tradability exists, but large lots and secondary turnover evidence do not prove live depth. No automatic cap is triggered. These are research judgments, not guarantees or calibrated return probabilities. [S1][S2][S6][S15][S16]

sections.title: 4. Business model and demand engine
sections.text:
Horizon converts scrap tyres and used rubber into natural, synthetic and EPDM reclaim rubber and crumb rubber for tyres, belts, mats, footwear, hoses and moulded products. Its production process combines shredding, granulation, softening and refining. EPR credits are sold to producers with regulatory recycling obligations. New facilities add pyrolysis-related outputs such as oil, char and recovered steel, which have different selling prices, end markets and capital economics. They must not be treated as identical tonnes of the existing reclaim business. [S1][S2][S8]

FY2026 physical-product sales were ₹46.32 crore and EPR sales ₹3.10 crore, or 6.28% of total revenue. The top ten customers represented a disclosed 35.20%, down from 50.03% in FY2024. The largest customer was the EPR buyer at 6.28%; the largest physical-products customer was about 5.01%. Top-ten supplier dependence was 42.29%. Customer and supplier relationships principally use purchase orders rather than binding long-term volume contracts. Diversification improves resilience, but repeat business is not contractual recurring revenue. [S2]

The company reports existing-unit production rising from 5,348 tonnes in FY2024 to 12,690 tonnes in FY2026 against 14,100-tonne capacity. This supports an underlying demand/throughput explanation for growth. It does not establish exact sold volumes, realized prices or incremental product margins because finished stocks also increased materially. [S2]

sections.title: 5. Competitive position and peer reality
sections.text:
The defensible advantages are practical process know-how, customer acceptance, scrap sourcing, established operations and environmental registrations. These matter operationally, but no strong proprietary technology, registered intellectual-property moat, long-term exclusive customer economics or persistent price premium was established. Competing suppliers can expand, and virgin-rubber prices, recycled-product spreads and imported scrap costs influence demand and profitability. [S2][S10]

Tinna is useful industry context, not a direct valuation template. Its primary July presentation reports approximately ₹546 crore FY2026 consolidated operating revenue and 17.1% EBITDA margin, versus 12.4% in FY2023. Its larger, diversified perimeter and products differ from Horizon's standalone business. This comparison demonstrates both an addressable market and serious scaled competition; it does not justify assigning Horizon Tinna's multiple or assuming Horizon's latest margin advantage is permanent. [S18][S19]

Horizon earns MOAT 4. Approval and relationship barriers are useful but contestable. EPR certificates depend on rules, registration, verified activity and demand; regulatory access alone is not an exclusive moat. No current market-share percentage or independently normalized peer valuation is invented. [S2][S10]

sections.title: 6. Demonstrated revenue growth
sections.text:
The preselected five-year revenue CAGR is 29.89%; the three-year CAGR is 36.00%. Physical revenue excluding EPR grew 28.22% annually over five years. The corresponding FY2024–26 physical revenues are ₹20.33, ₹32.86 and ₹46.32 crore. Thus, the headline is not explained only by the introduction of EPR revenue, although price/mix and the precise sold-tonnage bridge remain unknown. [S2][S3][S4][S5]

The original FY2020 revenue was ₹13.35 crore, almost the same as FY2021's ₹13.37 crore. There is no evidence for a mechanical pandemic-trough penalty after this cross-check. Restated FY2025 total revenue grew about 78.2% and FY2026 about 36.5%, while physical-product growth was approximately 61.7% and 40.9%. A single corrected H1 update is not enough for an additional sustained-trajectory point. REV remains 8, with no forecast, TAM or capex uplift. [S2][S3][S13]

The August presentation states Rajkot's first commercial sale occurred on 20 July. The later corrected update reportedly puts existing and new-unit utilization at 95% and 50%, and targets combined capacity of 86,800 tonnes. Those figures are management milestones, not contracted turnover. Mixed intermediate and final-product capacity cannot be multiplied by the legacy realization to manufacture a sales forecast. [S8][S12][S13][S14]

sections.title: 7. Growth quality and reinvestment economics
sections.text:
The earnings inflection is large: calculated operating EBITDA, excluding all other income and including all finance costs in the add-back, rises from ₹1.06 crore in FY2024 to ₹10.32 crore in FY2025 and ₹15.80 crore in FY2026. The FY2026 margin is about 32%. This differs from the issuer's reported EBITDA definition, which includes different finance/other-income treatments. The analysis does not carry historical forex income or tax credits into forecast operating profit. [S1][S2]

A normalized 26% tax and full financing-capital proxy give approximately 19.1% three-year incremental ROIC, compared with an assumed 14–18% capital-cost range. One-year incremental return is about 10.5% after the substantial capital build. Neither result is a mature new-plant cohort return: the denominator includes work in progress and the unresolved land advance, rather than flattering returns by excluding capital that shareholders financed. CAP 6 reflects promising historical improvement but mixed investment cohorts. [S1][S2]

The IPO added 5,269,200 shares, increasing the old issued share count by about 37.0%. FY2026 statutory EPS on today's shares is about ₹5.25, not the pre-IPO reported ₹7.19. Growth must eventually improve per-share cash earnings after expanded depreciation and working-capital requirements. No additional issuance is assumed in the model, but this is not a promise that future dilution cannot occur. [S1][S2][S8]

sections.title: 8. Governance, ownership and controls
sections.text:
The August presentation gives promoters and promoter group 69.97% ownership. Management has a long operating association with the business, but concentrated family control, the combined managing-director/CFO role and related-party property, rent, payroll and funding transactions warrant close stewardship review. Related-party status does not itself establish unfairness: the relevant tests are price, approvals, settlement, use and resulting returns. FY2026 related-party capital purchases were ₹1.96 crore and rent ₹0.63 crore, much of the latter capitalized during construction. [S1][S2][S8]

The financial-statement and internal-control audit opinions are unmodified. The accounts nevertheless disclose historical accounting corrections, differences between some bank stock/debtor returns and book amounts, and a database-level audit-trail limitation. Management attributes bank differences to purchase or receipt entries and the receivable provision. The March reconciliation's printed difference signs do not consistently match subtraction. These observations support a controls discount, not an allegation of fraud or quantified missing cash. [S1][S2]

The June prospectus also describes historical corporate-filing omissions and compounding applications submitted in March 2026. Subsequent final orders were not verified.

An auditor emphasis highlights the ₹6.25 crore property advance and bank-mortgage clearance, with a May addendum targeting a June sale deed; later completion was not established. No present breach, confirmed loss or diversion is asserted.

Current pledge quantity and an independent current rating rationale remain unverified. GOV 5 is conditional, not a clean-governance endorsement. [S1][S2]

sections.title: 9. Financial forensics and cash-claim audit
sections.text:
Restated three-year CFO/PAT is 0.73 and five-year conversion 0.77. FY2026 statutory CFO is ₹9.62 crore against PAT ₹10.25 crore; the prospectus restated versions are ₹10.09 crore and ₹10.50 crore. FY2025 statutory CFO of ₹0.48 crore also differs from restated ₹1.71 crore. Restatement notes identify prior-period benefits, stock, tax and asset-sale classification adjustments, but the full line-by-line revenue/cash regrouping is not completely explained. The two versions are shown rather than mixed to create a stronger cash score. [S1][S2]

Inventory increased to ₹10.02 crore, including ₹6.54 crore finished goods versus ₹1.01 crore previously. The ₹5.54 crore finished-stock movement reduces reported cost of goods sold; it is not itself a fictitious profit or an automatic write-off. It does make realized selling prices, aging and subsequent cash conversion essential. Net receivables fell to ₹3.38 crore. The separately disclosed ₹0.1436 crore old disputed receivable is already provided and is not impaired again. The EPR inventory note says recorded units have no recognized value because cost is nil, so no invented EPR inventory asset is added. [S1][S2]

All ₹64.8957 crore opening assets and claims reconcile. Ordinary WC includes supplier, employee, statutory and prepaid assets and trade/expense/payroll/customer-advance obligations. The model separately pays ₹0.3377 crore tax, ₹0.0059 crore accrued interest, ₹0.5052 crore capital creditor, ₹0.5675 crore capitalized rent and ₹0.4494 crore employee obligations. Current benefits are paid over twelve months and noncurrent benefits over the next forty-eight, rather than assumed immediately payable or silently erased by future payroll funding. [S1]

The ₹6.25 crore land advance stays unrecovered and receives no terminal cash credit. Deposits, deferred-tax assets and CSR credit are not treated as spendable cash. The appealed ₹8.52 lakh GST demand is conservatively settled in a sensitivity-conscious principal model, crediting the ₹0.40 lakh already deposited and paying only the balance. The small TDS demand is not duplicated on top of statutory WC unless it proves incremental. No model legal payment predicts an adverse ruling. [S1][S2]

sections.title: 10. Valuation and fully funded scenarios
sections.text:
At ₹139.50, current-share equity value is ₹272.24 crore and FY2026 statutory P/E is about 26.6×. March debt of ₹35.76 crore and cash of ₹0.15 crore cannot be described as October net debt after the IPO. The monitored June net proceeds were ₹49.7695 crore, entirely unused then: ₹6 crore for WC, ₹26.7 crore debt prepayment, ₹9.43 crore capex and ₹7.6395 crore general corporate purposes. The model preserves these pools and excludes unused object cash from terminal equity. It does not assume all proceeds are freely distributable. [S1][S2][S6][S7][S15]

The monthly model runs from audited March balances through 19 October 2031. All principal scenarios share the same estimated April–October path; future stress starts in November. H1 revenue is provisionally anchored to the corrected secondary ₹28.17 crore management update by shifting ₹2.83 crore of physical sales from the first half to the second without changing annual revenue. H1 product mix, margins and cash balances remain assumptions, not reported facts. The interpolated entry estimate is ₹5.56 crore free cash, ₹7.59 crore debt and ₹8.97 crore unspent object cash. These are assumptions, not reported October balances. Related-party debt is assumed paid in May from unrestricted operating cash before the June IPO, not from any IPO pool; exact historical settlement is unverified. Interest follows drawn debt and principal installments, and current tax is paid separately from legacy tax. Actual issued shares, not weighted-average EPS shares, determine value. [S1][S2][S6]

Base: FY2027 revenue ₹62.00 crore; then ₹77.05, ₹92.10, ₹105.78 and ₹118.19 crore through FY2031. Terminal annual run-rate revenue is ₹129.79 crore, not the partial FY2032 revenue in the cash model. Physical margin is 20% initially and 23% at maturity; EPR incremental margin is an explicit 95% assumption, not a disclosed segment result. Terminal EBITDA is ₹33.02 crore. At an assumed 10× exit, after cash, debt and remaining claims, equity is ₹398.09 crore, or ₹203.99 per share. No dividends are assumed. Dated IRR is 7.90%.

Bear: slower physical growth, approximately halved EPR revenue, 15% physical margin, 75 inventory days, 55 receivable days and 7× exit give ₹51.52 per share and −18.07% IRR. Bull: much faster scaling, 26% mature physical margin, larger maintenance/reinvestment and 13× exit give ₹460.98 and 27.01%. These are scenarios, not probability-weighted price targets. All three fund the modeled cash path; an unfunded sensitivity receives no shareholder IRR.

The base includes the full ₹4 crore legacy completion commitment, quoted ₹11.423 crore new machinery, assumed ₹1 crore incidental costs and ₹2.056 crore gross input GST. Potential budget overlap is a separate alternative, not silently netted. GST stays unmonetized in principal cases; a 24-month utilization alternative is provided. Existing capital creditors are paid without buying the same assets twice. Depreciation rises with commissioning; a 15× earnings cross-check gives only about ₹162 per share at exit, below the base EV/EBITDA result.

The base supports present entry values of ₹115.76, ₹101.43 and ₹89.17 at 12%, 15% and 18% required returns. The 15% hurdle requires 14.53× terminal EBITDA on the base path or about 27% annual physical growth after FY2027 at 10×. A constant 18% physical margin reduces return to about 3.22%; 15% produces approximately flat nominal return. The attractive bull result therefore cannot substitute for a defensible margin of safety.

sections.title: 11. Bear case, survivability and failure boundaries
sections.text:
The credible no-rescue test starts with an annualized ₹44 crore physical-sales run rate from November, zero EPR, 12% initial physical margin, 75-day inventory and 60-day receivables. Those stresses are linked to the disclosed legacy revenue, low historical margins, current inventory intensity, former collection cycle, lack of volume contracts and regulatory-credit dependence, rather than an arbitrary stack of maximum losses. It preserves existing debt, capital commitments, tax and employee claims. Optional remaining unplaced machinery is curtailed; its earmarked pool stays restricted. [S1][S2][S6]

This case survives without a new facility, rescue issue or assumed refinancing draw. Minimum modeled free cash after the cutoff is about ₹4.00 crore. A countercase completing all remaining growth machinery also survives, although with lower headroom and shareholder value. Survival therefore supports Conditional G3 rather than a forced Fail. It does not support high downside protection: severe-case terminal equity is only about ₹29.33 per share.

The base construction period is considerably tighter, with minimum post-cutoff free cash about ₹1.27 crore. A 25% increase in the remaining new-project cost assumptions produces a ₹0.1789 crore monthly gap beginning in November; no IRR is presented for that unfunded path. Pacing the remaining machinery or demonstrating existing committed finance could resolve it, but neither is silently assumed. Delaying the still-unpaid portion to March, without paying it twice, is separately funded. This is a modeled execution boundary, not evidence of an actual default.

Finished-stock and net-receivable haircuts, zero future deposit interest, 12% floating debt cost, no prepaid-IPO reimbursement, capex overlap and a ₹1 crore unquantified compliance-cost sensitivity are explicit. The no-reimbursement variant produces a small historical June timing gap in the assumed bridge, not an asserted present-day funding failure; it is not used to fail the forward survivability gate. Impairment reduces recoverable stock, is added back once as noncash and requires replacement funding once. Current permit renewals, title clearance and actual October bank balances remain evidence needed before upgrading resilience. [S1][S2]

sections.title: 12. Multibagger feasibility
sections.text:
A threefold share return over five years requires approximately 24.6% annualized growth in equity value; fivefold requires 38.0%, and tenfold 58.5%. With today's shares, terminal equity would need roughly ₹817 crore, ₹1,361 crore and ₹2,722 crore respectively. At a 10× EBITDA exit and the base terminal cash/debt bridge, those outcomes need approximately ₹74.9 crore, ₹129.3 crore and ₹265.5 crore EBITDA, compared with the base ₹33.0 crore.

The bull case exceeds threefold only with rapid multi-year scaling, stronger margins and a 13× rather than 10× exit. That is conceivable execution optionality, not a supported base outcome. Fivefold or tenfold requires much larger operating scale, capital, customer access and cash realization than the evidence currently establishes. The announced 86,800-tonne combined capacity is not sufficient proof because the products, intermediates, yields, prices and utilization differ. [S2][S8]

The real milestones are collected incremental gross profit, adequate return on fully funded new assets, no hidden dilution requirement and durable operating permissions. A large TAM or small starting market capitalization alone does not earn a multibagger classification.

sections.title: 13. Monitoring and falsification
sections.text:
The next useful evidence is signed H1 financials and the corrected operating update, including receivables, finished goods, cash, debt and IPO object deployment. A revenue headline without collected cash cannot resolve the thesis. Reconcile the prospectus and statutory comparative presentations and verify the database audit trail and bank-return remediation. [S1][S2][S6][S12]

Operational tests are verified commissioning, product sale volumes, plant-level margins after startup costs, current consents to operate, new-capex invoices, and how much of the older ₹4 crore commitment overlaps the new machinery plan. EPR sales should be tracked separately from physical operations and matched to receipts, not assumed to recur indefinitely. [S2][S8][S10][S11]

Falsifiers include repeated finished-stock accumulation without collections, new cash needs funded by unannounced dilution, lasting physical margins nearer the low historical range, material recurring reporting failures, or adverse legal/title outcomes that consume the construction buffer. Positive evidence would be sustained cash conversion above earnings without supplier stretching and new assets earning returns above the stated capital-cost range. These are review triggers, not an automatic trading or monitoring instruction.

sections.title: 14. Classification and implementation
sections.text:
Classification: speculative, execution-dependent expansion; weak attraction at the stated price and hurdle. Revenue growth is evidenced, funding is substantially better after the IPO, but economic durability and cash conversion lag the headline capacity narrative. The score does not imply that a marginal cross-company difference is economically significant.

The conservative 60-session low-price turnover bound averages ₹89.82 lakh and has median ₹47.88 lakh. At the lower denominator, a ₹5 lakh exit needs about 2.09 theoretical days at 5% participation, 5.22 days at 2% and 1.04 days at 10%. The latest 20-session median lower bound is ₹73.18 lakh, implying 1.37 days at 5%. These are lower-bound price×volume capacity calculations, not guaranteed executable turnover. [S15]

Lot size changes implementation materially: two lots cost ₹334,800 while three cost ₹502,200, slightly above the reference position. One lot fits 5% of the low-bound daily turnover on only 40 of 60 sessions and 15 of the latest 20. All observed sessions are post-listing; no prelisting days were zero-filled. Unknown live spread, depth, circuit-side liquidity and current BSE restrictions prevent turning this analysis into an execution instruction. [S15][S16][S17]

sections.title: 15. Sources, assumptions and what remains unknown
sections.text:
Primary foundations are the issuer's annual reports, final prospectus, signed June IPO monitoring report, operating presentation and environmental certificate. The scanned historical statements and decisive FY2026 faces were visually checked. The full source ledger distinguishes verified disclosures (V), reproducible calculations (C), management statements (M) and analyst assumptions (A), with dates and locators. Tinna is context only; the secondary corrected H1 headline and BSE market history retain explicit limitations. [S1][S2][S3][S4][S5][S6][S8][S10][S12][S15][S18]

The forecast assumes a 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle, 26% current cash tax, 9% main floating borrowing cost, stated contractual vehicle interest, no new rescue financing, no future dividend and no terminal recovery of the land advance or unmonetized tax/deposit assets. Post-March cash dates, future margins, commissioning, capex incidentals and exit multiples are not issuer facts. A full monthly operating/financing ledger, annual aggregation, complete opening-claim map, terminal equity bridge and independent arithmetic QA accompany the conclusions.

Unresolved items include actual October balances and object usage; exact H1 signed correction; new-line operating consents and short-lived permit renewals; land-deed status; later corporate-compounding and tax outcomes; product realization and sold-volume decomposition; current pledge and rating evidence; and live market depth. Those gaps limit confidence, but do not justify inventing either a clean bill of health or unsupported misconduct. The research is conditional and should be updated when decisive primary evidence changes.

evidence.limitation: Later outcomes not verified. Filing omissions and pending title clearance do not establish misconduct, a present unlicensed operation or a confirmed loss.

evidence.limitation: A consent to establish is not a current consent to operate. Several short-lived import, metrology and stability approvals need current renewals; no breach inferred from an older prospectus.

evidence.locator: Exact formulas retained in financial calculations
evidence.limitation: Capital proxy includes CWIP and stranded advance economics; normalized 26% tax is an assumption, not reported tax. March EV is explicitly stale for October.
evidence.formula: Growth = (end/start)^(1/years) − 1; NOPAT = (PBT + finance cost − other income) × 0.74; IC = equity + debt − cash; incremental ROIC = ΔNOPAT/ΔIC.

evidence.locator: Full dated operating, tax, capex, borrowing and object-pool model
evidence.limitation: Forecast uncertainty is High. All principal cases share the modeled pre-cutoff path; stress begins November. No prospective raise, refinancing draw or canceled-object cash rescue.
evidence.formula: Equity = exit EBITDA × multiple + unrestricted cash − debt − remaining legacy claims; XIRR uses dated per-share cash flows and actual issued shares.

evidence.locator: Historical rows and official lot size
evidence.limitation: Not live bid/ask depth, actual exchange turnover or a suitable user allocation.
evidence.formula: Low-bound turnover = daily low × volume; illustrative exit days = ₹500,000 / (participation × min(mean, median)).

evidence.locator: July presentation pp37–38
evidence.limitation: Larger diversified consolidated peer, unlike Horizon standalone. Not a like-for-like valuation multiple or a verification of Horizon margins.

limitations: Actual October balance sheet, IPO object deployment, bank prepayment and project invoices are not verified. The bridge from audited March and monitored June to the cutoff is an assumption, not a current cash confirmation.
The signed 19 October H1 correction remains inaccessible. Secondary summaries are corroboration only; no H1 cash flow, segment profit or audited utilization was established.

Earlier original and prospectus-restated profits/cash classifications differ. Both versions are retained; the line-by-line revenue and CFO regrouping is not fully reconciled, although cash faces and key claim partitions are bounded.

Exact product sale volumes, price/mix effects, EPR-specific collections, new-plant operating costs and mature incremental returns remain unavailable. Production is not sold volume, and mixed plant tonnages are not additive revenues.
Later corporate-compounding, GST-appeal, property-title and permit-renewal outcomes were not located. No misconduct, current license breach or final adverse liability is inferred.
Unplaced new-machinery budgets exclude taxes and incidental costs. The overlap with the existing ₹4 crore commitment, actual timing and current facility amortization need confirmation.
Secondary BSE histories do not verify actual traded value, circuit-side executable depth or current surveillance. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is not a recommended position.
Current pledge balances and an independent current credit-rating rationale were not found; lack of a search result is not evidence that no rating or encumbrance exists.
Forecast uncertainty is High; exit multiples, margins, tax, capex timing and the 14–18% capital-cost comparison are analytical assumptions, not assured returns.

GOV.reason: Unmodified audit and transparent prospectus disclosure are positive, but recurring historical filing, accounting and audit-trail weaknesses and related-party capital/rent exposure prevent a strong stewardship rating. No fraud, diversion or present default is inferred.

MOAT.reason: Operating know-how, approvals and buyer relationships have practical value, but commoditized reclaimed materials, non-binding orders and larger peers limit evidence of persistent pricing or switching power. EPR access is regulatory, not proprietary.

REV.reason: A preselected five-year reported revenue CAGR of 29.9% starts at 8. Physical revenue excluding EPR grows about 28.2%, and FY2020/FY2021 are nearly flat, so growth is not merely new credit revenue or a pandemic trough. No trajectory uplift is taken; new-line persistence is not proven.

DUR.reason: Recycled-rubber demand and funded new facilities provide accessible runway, but large mixed-capacity figures, environmental approvals, customer qualification and lack of a binding backlog constrain certainty. November capacity is a target, not sold output.

CAP.reason: Three-year normalized incremental return including expansion capital is about 19.1%, above the assumed 14–18% capital-cost range, but one-year incremental return is about 10.5%. New CWIP and pyrolysis cohorts have yet to earn mature returns; high return ratios that exclude this capital are rejected.

CASH.reason: Restated cumulative CFO/PAT is about 0.73 over three years and 0.77 over five. Latest conversion improves but finished inventory absorbs substantial cash; statutory CFO is lower than restated. Collection improvement is real evidence, not proof of durable cash discipline.

BAL.reason: Received IPO proceeds can materially deleverage and fund a credible no-rescue survival case. Object restrictions, legacy claims, a stranded land advance, unverified actual October cash and tight peak construction funding keep resilience conditional.

EXEC.reason: Existing-unit production and utilization improved materially and Rajkot began commercial sales. New pyrolysis operations and the final expansion remain early-stage; exact commissioning and funded cash returns, rather than capacity announcements, determine whether execution is repeatable.

EARN.reason: Physical volume and operating profit grew, not just other income. Yet EPR, substantial finished-goods accumulation, restatements and impending depreciation of new assets make 32% historical operating EBITDA margins an unsafe perpetual assumption. IPO dilution lowers current-share EPS.

R.reason: Funded base XIRR 7.8973% minus the 15% equity hurdle is −7.1027 percentage points, within the canonical −10 to −7 band. No arbitrary multiple premium is added for capacity targets.

D.reason: The funded bear terminal price near ₹51.52 implies about 63% capital loss from ₹139.50; severe survival economics are worse. Operations can survive without rescue while shareholders still suffer substantial valuation loss.

P.reason: The 15% hurdle needs about 14.53× exit EBITDA on the base operating path or approximately 27% annual physical growth after FY2027 at 10×. That requires stronger sustained execution than the base; the current quote offers limited allowance for margin or ramp misses.

L.reason: The conservative 60-day low-bound turnover implies 2.09 days at 5% participation, starting at 7. A ₹167,400 lot fits that participation on only 40 of 60 sessions; the recently listed, concentrated register and unavailable live spread/depth justify one point lower.
